Bayside and offshore

Event Planners in Redlands

Part of Redland City is on the mainland and part of it is across the water, and an island event runs on a ferry timetable rather than a run sheet. Tell us whether your event is bayside or offshore, along with the date and guest number, and planners covering both can respond.

Get event planning quotesHow planning works
  • Part of it is offshoreNorth Stradbroke and the southern bay islands sit inside Redland City.
  • Ferries run to a timetableCleveland and Redland Bay are the mainland departure points for the islands.
  • Bay, not surfThe mainland foreshore is mangrove and calm water rather than open beach.

Everything for an island event crosses the water on somebody else's timetable.

The chairs, the food, the staff, the ice and most of the guests. Miss a sailing and there is no second option, which is why the schedule is built from the timetable outwards.

Redland City is bayside, and a genuine part of it is offshore. The council area takes in North Stradbroke Island and the Southern Moreton Bay Islands at Russell and Macleay, all of which are reached by ferry or barge from Cleveland and Redland Bay. That is the fact that separates it from every neighbouring council, and it is the first thing to raise with event planners in Redlands, because an island event and a mainland one are different jobs with different risks.

On the mainland the character is calm water rather than surf. The foreshore from Wellington Point through Ormiston and Victoria Point down to Redland Bay faces mangroves, sandflats and the bay islands beyond, so the light is soft, the water is flat and the tide decides how much of the foreshore you actually have.

In and around Redlands

What are you planning in Redlands?

The first question a planner should ask you here is whether anything has to cross the water. Everything downstream, from the budget to the finish time, follows the answer.

Start with

Weddings

Island weddings are the reason a lot of people look here, and they are logistics before they are styling. Guests, staff, hire, catering and flowers all cross to a timetable, and most guest lists end up staying overnight because the last service back leaves before the party would.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Mainland parties at Alexandra Hills, Thornlands and Capalaba are ordinary suburban jobs with generous yards. Island parties are not, even small ones, because a birthday for 40 people still means a barge booking for the hire and a plan for anyone who misses the boat.

Find planners

Corporate events

Most corporate work here is mainland and daytime: training, community forums, presentations and end of year functions around Cleveland and Capalaba. An island offsite is possible and memorable, but treat the crossing as part of the programme rather than as travel time, and book the return sailing first.

Find planners

Engagement parties

These are usually mainland and usually at a family home, which around Wellington Point and Ormiston can mean a yard that backs onto the water. Two questions come first: what the tide is doing at the hour of the party, and where 60 cars go on a quiet residential street.

Find planners

Proposals

The bay faces east, so sunrise from the foreshore at Wellington Point or Victoria Point is the strong option and it is quiet at that hour. Check the tide before the time. At low water the sandflats run a long way out and the shoreline you photographed is nowhere near the sea.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Wakes, christenings and milestone birthdays mostly stay close to home on the mainland. Where the family is on Russell or Macleay, the guest number is effectively set by the ferry rather than by the room, so confirm the sailing capacity before you invite anyone.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Redlands?

For anything across the water, coordination is the floor rather than the budget option. Someone has to own the manifest, the barge booking and the last sailing, and that someone cannot be a guest who is also getting married that day.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Budget built and tracked
  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

Partial planning

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

  • Picks up from where you are
  • Fills the supplier gaps
  • Tidies the budget
  • Builds the run sheet
  • Hands back a plan you can follow

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day
  • Handles what goes sideways

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Redlands

If your event is on an island, the first three questions decide whether it works at all. The fourth applies to the mainland foreshore and catches people out just as often.

No. 01

Ask how many island events they have delivered

This is the question. An island job needs a barge booking for the hire, a passenger manifest, a delivery window that fits the sailing schedule and a contingency for a service that does not run. Ask a planner which islands they have worked on, in what month, and what went wrong. Enthusiasm is not experience, and the water does not care which it is.

No. 02

Put the last service on the run sheet in writing

The final sailing back to Cleveland or Redland Bay is a hard deadline, not a guide. It sets your finish time, your speeches, your last drink and the moment the crew has to start packing. Ask where it sits in the schedule and what happens to anyone who misses it, because on an island the answer has to be a bed rather than a taxi.

No. 03

Ask what the hire costs to get across

Freight is the line people forget. Tables, chairs, a marquee, a generator, a cool room and the flowers all travel by barge, and the charge applies in both directions, days apart. Ask for the delivery and collection cost stated separately from the hire, and ask what happens if the return barge is full on the Sunday.

No. 04

Check the tide against your ceremony hour

On the mainland foreshore the tide changes what the site is. At low water the bay pulls back across the sandflats and the view from Wellington Point or Redland Bay is mud rather than water, which is fine if you expected it and a shock if you did not. Ask the planner to check the tide for the exact hour before the date is set.

Nothing about an island event is difficult. It is just that none of it can be late.

On the ground

What the water adds to every decision

Two thirds of this page is about the crossing, because that is what makes Redlands different. The third part is about the tide, which shapes the mainland foreshore just as firmly.

The islands are part of the city, not a day trip

North Stradbroke Island sits off Cleveland and the Southern Moreton Bay Islands sit off Redland Bay, and all of them are inside this council area. They are reached by passenger ferry and by vehicle barge, which are separate services with separate timetables and separate bookings. That distinction matters more than anything else in the plan. Guests can usually walk onto a passenger service. A truck of hire equipment, a cool room and a generator need the barge, and the barge has capacity limits and cut off times that are set months before your date.

An island run sheet is written backwards from the last sailing

Work out when the final service leaves, then build every other hour from it. That single number decides the ceremony time, the length of the speeches, when the band stops and when the crew starts loading out. It also decides accommodation, because a guest list that cannot leave has to sleep somewhere, and island beds are limited and go early for the cool dry months. Add a contingency for weather, since a cancelled or delayed sailing is a real possibility rather than a remote one.

The mainland shore is bay, not beach

From Wellington Point through Ormiston, Thorneside and Victoria Point down to Redland Bay, the foreshore faces mangroves, sandflats and calm water. It is a softer setting than an ocean beach and the light is different, but the tide runs the site.

  • Check the tide for the exact hour, not the day
  • Expect sandflats and mud at low water, not a shoreline
  • Mangroves bring insects at dusk in the warmer months
  • Public foreshore reserve needs council approval for an organised event

Questions

Planning an event in Redlands

What does an event planner charge in Redlands?

A mainland event is priced like any other suburban job, on scope and guest number. An island event is not. Barge bookings, a passenger manifest, freight in both directions, accommodation for guests who cannot leave and a weather contingency all add hours, and most planners quote the crossing separately. Ask for the two parts split out so you can see what the water is actually costing you.

How does an event on North Stradbroke Island actually work?

Everything crosses from Cleveland on a timetable, and the timetable runs the day. Guests travel on the passenger service, while the hire, the catering, the generator and any vehicles go by barge with a booking made well in advance. Build the run sheet backwards from the last return sailing, then decide who is staying overnight, because island accommodation is limited and books out early for the cool dry months from April to September.

What happens if the ferry is cancelled?

Plan for it before the date rather than on the day, because weather on the bay does stop services. The workable answers are all decided in advance: a second sailing option, a night's accommodation held for the crew and any guests who cannot get back, deliveries brought across a day early rather than on the morning, and one person with the authority to make the call. Ask your planner which of those they build in as standard.

Can we hold a ceremony on the foreshore at Wellington Point or Victoria Point?

Usually yes with council approval, since the foreshore is public reserve, and the conditions generally cover numbers, marquees, vehicles, chairs, amplified sound and alcohol. The local variable is the tide. This is bay rather than surf, so at low water the sandflats extend a long way out and the water in your photographs is somewhere else. Check the tide for the exact hour before you set the ceremony time, then apply for the permit.

Do mainland suppliers travel to Russell and Macleay?

Some do and some do not, and the honest ones will tell you which they are. The barge from Redland Bay adds a booking, a cost and a schedule to what is otherwise a 20 minute run, and it applies again for collection. Ask a planner which of their suppliers already work the southern bay islands, and get the freight cost quoted separately from the hire so you can compare two quotes properly.

How far ahead should we book an island event?

Longer than a mainland one, and the reason is beds rather than venues. Island accommodation is limited, so a guest list that has to stay overnight needs rooms held before the date is announced, and the cool dry Saturdays from April to September go first. Twelve months is a sensible target for a wedding with a large travelling guest list. Barge bookings and a passenger manifest can follow once the numbers are firm.
